## Natural history notes

A small lynx spider characterized by its slender body, long spiny legs, and tan to grayish-brown coloration that helps it blend into sandy or grassy vegetation. In Florida, it is found in open habitats such as scrub, sandhills, fields, prairies, and low vegetation, where it actively moves through plants or along the ground in search of prey. It does not build a prey-capturing web; instead, it relies on speed, vision, and ambush-style hunting to capture small insects and other arthropods.
